results.title: How to Combine Archival Data Analysis with Surveys and Interviews
results.content: # How can you combine archival data analysis with surveys and interviews for research? Archival data analysis is a research method that uses existing data sources, such as historical records, official documents, media archives, or databases, to answer research questions. Therefore, combining archival data analysis with other methods, such as surveys and interviews, can enhance the validity, reliability, and richness of your research findings. In this article, you will learn how to combine archival data analysis with surveys and interviews for research. The first step is to choose a research question that can be addressed by both archival data analysis and surveys or interviews. Archival data analysis can be limited by data availability and potential bias, while surveys and interviews can lack historical context and representativeness. Triangulate findings: Combine archival data analysis with surveys and interviews to triangulate your findings and enhance the validity, reliability, and richness of your research. The third step is to design and conduct surveys or interviews that can complement, confirm, or challenge the findings from the archival data analysis. You also need to consider how to align your survey or interview questions with your research question and your archival data analysis results. You also need to compare and contrast your survey or interview data with your archival data analysis results, and to identify any similarities, differences, gaps, or contradictions. The goal of this step is to answer your research question and to explain how your archival data analysis and your survey or interview data support, extend, or challenge your findings. The goal of this step is to communicate your research findings and contributions to your audience, and to demonstrate how you have combined archival data analysis with surveys or interviews for research. A researcher may also corroborate the archival data with the data collected from field surveys and interviews with a focus group. Analysis of data from these sources may lead to findings that are authentic, reliable, valid, and more importantly relevant to the research question. Search for other works by this author on:. George Washington University, Washington, DC, USA. Search for other works by this author on:. *Communist and Post-Communist Studies* (2025) 58 (4): 184–198. Chapman, Raushan Zhandayeva; Elite Narratives and State Response to Kazakhstan’s *Qandy Qantar* Protests. **Communist and Post-Communist Studies** 1 December 2025; 58 (4): 184–198. Weeks before Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Russian-led CSTO forces intervened in Kazakhstan’s January 2022 Qandy Qantar protests at the government’s request. Many observers predicted this intervention would deepen Kazakhstan’s dependence on Russia, leading to support for Moscow’s invasion. Yet Kazakhstan’s subsequent actions defied these expectations. This study examines how the Kazakhstani government strategically framed and managed domestic unrest within a shifting geopolitical context, from initially emphasizing foreign threats to justify CSTO intervention to later reframing reforms as necessary for protecting sovereignty amid global upheaval. Through analysis of evolving state narratives and policy decisions, we demonstrate how great power-centric analysis overlooks the sophisticated ways states navigate asymmetric relationships. This case illustrates the importance of examining how smaller states in asymmetric relationships strategically manage both domestic and international pressures to advance their interests. © 2025 by The Regents of the University of California. results.title: The narrative trap: How we can misread China | Lowy Institute
results.content: Unverified claims about Beijing’s intentions can gain momentum precisely because China's opacity makes them impossible to disprove. When President Xi Jinping disappears from public view for a period of time, speculation surges about his health or even a possible coup (Pedro Pardo/AFP via Getty Images). For instance, President Xi Jinping disappears from public view for a period of time, and speculation surges about his health or even a possible coup. Few figures in China attract more speculation than Xi himself. A persistent narrative in recent years has been the so-called “2027 invasion deadline”, the idea that China will move on Taiwan by that year. The examples from Xi’s rumoured downfall to a fabricated submarine disaster to timelines for war all illustrate the risks of treating uncertainty as potential truths. A clearer view of China will come not from tidy narratives but from analytical discipline: recognising the limits of what we know, distinguishing possibility from probability, and remaining alert to how fear and expectation shape the lens through which we interpret Beijing’s behaviour.

results.title: Snapdragon X Elite laptops from Dell are launching soon, leaked docs ...
results.content: # Snapdragon X Elite laptops from Dell are launching soon, leaked docs claim nearly double the battery life ## The Arm-based chips could be costing Dell half as much as Intel's Snapdragon X Elite laptops from Dell are launching soon, leaked docs claim nearly double the battery life **In context:** Recent leaks have started to support Qualcomm's bold claims about the capabilities of its upcoming Snapdragon X Elite processors. The most significant leak yet comes from Dell, one of the manufacturers expected to release a line of Snapdragon laptops soon. The upcoming XPS laptops, among others, are expected to launch a new phase of Arm Windows PCs leveraging generative AI. A leaked internal document from Dell has revealed a lengthy outline of the company's plans for XPS laptops over the next few years, including a set of Snapdragon-powered models launching soon. Potentially the most significant takeaway from the 311-page Dell document is the dramatic advantage the Snapdragon X Elite holds over Intel processors in terms of battery life and cost. Snapdragon maker Qualcomm claims its new Arm-powered chips can outperform some of the best mobile CPUs from Intel and AMD, and leaks have begun to bear that out. Dell estimates that the Snapdragon powering its upcoming XPS 13 laptop achieves a 68 percent to 98 percent battery life improvement when playing videos compared to an Intel Alder Lake-P CPU. Furthermore, the Snapdragon processors might cost Dell half as much as Raptor Lake Intel chips, potentially lowering prices for consumers or giving the company elbow room in other areas. Meanwhile, sources recently provided Windows Report with more information on the XPS 13 Plus and an upcoming Snapdragon-powered Inspiron laptop. However, the Cupertino giant recently introduced M4 in its newest iPads and is expected to reveal M4-powered Macs later this year, intensifying 2024's Arm AI PC race. Looking further ahead, Arm recently suggested that Qualcomm isn't the only chipmaker developing Arm-based processors for Windows PCs. Arm itself plans to introduce AI processors next year. Moreover, the leaked Dell roadmap suggests that second and third-generation Snapdragon X chips could emerge between 2025 and 2027.
